Thanks for making time. Let me describe the role, because the title on the advertisement does not tell the whole story. We are looking for someone who can own pricing across eight countries, not someone who runs a team of analysts. The person we hire will report to the chief commercial officer, and the mandate is to build a model that works at SKU level in markets which are very different from each other. The candidate we want has done this at least once before, in a business where price is the main lever. One more thing. The role, which is new, does not exist in any other company in the group. So the first six months are about defining the scope, not delivering a number.

Quick debrief on the two candidates we saw this morning. The first one, who came from a consultancy, gave the cleaner presentation. He described a framework which is well known, and he described it very well. The second candidate was harder to follow, but he talked about a model that he actually built himself, in a business where the data was terrible. And when I asked him what he would do differently, he answered without defending himself. For me that is the difference. The person we need is not the one who explains a framework best. It is the one who has lived the problem the framework is trying to solve.

First, the company writes the specification that describes the role. Then it agrees the criteria which candidates have to meet. After that, the recruiter contacts the people who match the profile. Next, the panel interviews the candidates that reached the final stage. Finally, the team runs the due diligence before the offer is signed.
